page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-256 is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance is powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz. It allocates 32 dedicated physical cores and 64 vCPUs utilizing simultaneous multithreading with two threads per core. The hardware configuration includes 256 GB of system memory, providing 4 GB of RAM per vCPU to maintain a balanced 1:4 compute-to-memory ratio.

Hardware expansion is characterized by the absence of bundled local storage and hardware acceleration. The instance contains zero GPUs and provides no local NVMe scratch disks, requiring persistent block storage to be provisioned over the network. One complimentary public IPv4 address is included. Because the instance features dedicated core allocation rather than burstable or shared CPU threads, multi-threaded workloads experience consistent CPU execution without noisy-neighbor contention.

The 64 vCPU and 256 GB memory configuration suits tasks requiring balanced memory allocation and high concurrent thread counts. Primary workload fits include enterprise web application clusters, container management nodes, batch data processing, continuous integration and deployment pipelines, and transactional database services running on attached network storage.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-256 is a balanced, general-purpose virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture and powered by an AMD EPYC 9J45 processor running at 2.7 GHz. The configuration provides 32 dedicated physical cores mapped to 64 vCPUs across two threads per core, coupled with 256 GB of total memory, establishing a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio. This server configuration does not include local disk storage or specialized GPU acceleration, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent I/O workloads. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned for network connectivity. With dedicated CPU allocation preventing neighbor contention, this instance offers predictable processing density for moderate-to-heavy concurrent workloads. VM.Standard.E6.Ax.Flex.32-256 is targeted at enterprise web serving, container clustering, CI/CD build environments, ETL data pipelines, and distributed databases operating over networked storage.
